deep.reconstruction:
This page states the master theorem of a draft section on symmetrically normed operator ideals between Hilbert spaces.

Setting. N is a 'norme de Schatten' on R^(N), the finitely supported sequences: in modern terms a symmetric gauge function in von Neumann's sense, i.e. a norm invariant under permutations and sign changes. N° is its dual gauge. ℓ^N is the maximal sequence space {x : sup_n N(x_1..x_n) < ∞}, and ℓ_N is the closure of R^(N) in it. E and F are Hilbert spaces (Grothendieck crossed out 'Banach'). L_0(E,F) denotes the compact operators and t_i(u) the singular numbers (s-numbers).

① Definitions and identification.
- (18): for compact u, N(u) = N((t_i(u))).
- (19): for arbitrary bounded u, N(u) = sup |Tr uv| over finite-rank v ∈ F'⊗E with N°(v) ≤ 1. This is the duality definition, and on compact operators it agrees with (18).
- L^N(E,F) = {u : N(u) < ∞} is a Banach space under N. This is the maximal symmetrically normed ideal, Schatten's 'σ-type' cross-space.
- For compact u, u ∈ L^N iff (t_i(u)) ∈ ℓ^N.
- The closure L_N(E,F) of the finite-rank operators in L^N consists of the compact u with (t_i(u)) ∈ ℓ_N. This is the minimal (separable) ideal.
- The previous page shows L^N ⊂ L_0 unless N ~ N_∞.

② Adjoints and the ideal property.
- (20): N(u) = N(u*), so the classes are stable under adjoints.
- (21): N(vu) ≤ ||v|| N(u) and N(vu) ≤ N(v) ||u||. This is the two-sided ideal property.
- There is a garbled remark that these spaces generalize ℓ^N and ℓ_N, and that N is a convex function (likely of hermitian operators in L_0(E)).

③ Hölder-type inequality.
- (22)–(23): if N(xy) ≤ N'(x) N''(y) for sequences, then N(vu) ≤ N'(v) N''(u). Hence the corresponding products of operators lie in L^N, and in L_N if one factor lies in the small ideal.
- (24): in particular ||vu||_1 ≤ N(u) N°(v), so L^N · L^{N°} ⊂ L^1 (trace class).
- (25): |Tr vu| ≤ N(u) N°(v). This yields the trace pairing used on the next page to show that the dual of L_N(E,F) is L^{N°}(F,E), and to characterize reflexivity.

What the proofs would use. The finite-rank case rests on Ky Fan / Horn majorization: the singular values of vu are weakly majorized by the decreasingly ordered product s(v)s(u). The general case follows by finite-rank compressions p v u p, exactly as sketched on the previous page.

Purpose. This is a systematic theory of the ideals C_N (Schatten–von Neumann cross-spaces), feeding Grothendieck's tensor-product programme: Hilbert-space instances of tensor norms and their duality, and reflexivity of operator ideals.
errors: (23) is written N(vu) ≤ N'(v)N''(u), but the consequence is stated as u ∈ L^{N'}, v ∈ L^{N''}. The roles of N' and N'' are swapped relative to (23); harmless by symmetry of the hypothesis only if N(xy) is symmetric in its roles, which it is for commuting sequences.
Domains: 'v ∈ L^{N''}(E,F)' should read v ∈ L^{N''}(F,G), and 'vu ∈ L^N(E,F)' should read L^N(E,G).
(21) is written N(uv) with u ∈ L(E,F), v ∈ L(F,G); the composable product is vu. This is notational.

Hypothesis (22) must be read for sequences, so that it applies to decreasingly rearranged singular-value sequences. The passage from (22) to (23) needs the Horn/Ky Fan weak log-majorization of s(vu) by s(v)s(u). This is not written on this page.
Stating L^N(E,F) ⇔ L^N(F',E') via adjoints for Hilbert spaces implicitly uses conjugate-linear identifications. This is fine, but unstated.

ideas.what: Symmetric-gauge-function norms on operators: N(u) = N(singular values), extended to bounded operators by trace duality against finite-rank operators
ideas.modern_name: Symmetrically normed ideals S_Φ / S_Φ^(0) (maximal and separable ideals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann (1937), Schatten (1950, 'A Theory of Cross-Spaces'), Calkin (1941); systematized by Gohberg–Krein (1965)
ideas.where_published: Related material: Grothendieck, 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace', Sém. Bourbaki 1955; Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955) discusses Schatten classes

ideas.what: Characterization: compact u lies in L^N iff its s-numbers are in ℓ^N; the closure of finite-rank operators corresponds to ℓ_N

ideas.modern_name: Generalized Hölder inequality for symmetrically normed ideals (via Horn/Ky Fan majorization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ky Fan (1951), Horn (1950), Gohberg–Krein; Schatten for trace duality

ideas.what: Ideal property and adjoint invariance: N(vu) ≤ ||v|| N(u), N(u*) = N(u)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, competent write-up of the theory of symmetrically normed operator ideals: definition by trace duality, maximal and minimal ideals, Hölder inequality and trace pairing. All of it is essentially in Schatten (1950) and was later systematized by Gohberg–Krein. Grothendieck's own 1955 Bourbaki talk went further, to von Neumann algebras. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'L^ε_N(E,F)' and 'L^#_{N''}(E,F)' are almost certainly just L_N(E,F) and L_{N''}(F,G); the marks are stray strokes or corrections.
In ③, 'v ∈ L^{N''}(E,F)' in the image context should read v ∈ L^{N''}(F,G).

The garbled sentence after (21) seems to say that these spaces generalize ℓ^N (resp. ℓ_N), with ℓ^N-type spaces as the commutative/diagonal case. The arrow note likely reads 'N(u) est fonction convexe sur l'ensemble des [opérateurs hermitiens] dans L_0(E)'.
Margin '?' in red next to ② concerns the adjoint statement u ∈ L^N(E,F) ⇔ u* ∈ L^N(F',E').
